newsitem.title: LATVIA: Baltic markets mixed in short week of trade.
newsitem.headline: Baltic markets mixed in short week of trade.

text.p: Estonia's liquid market charged out of the four-day holiday weekend straight at red rags but the bears in Latvia and Lithuania showed few signs of hibernating.
Estonia's market was pushed up by acquisition announcements and merger rumours and dealers saw further gains ahead of six-month results from the banking sector.
But Latvia and Lithuania did not really pick up until Friday and the outlook for both was mixed.
ESTONIA
The Talse index rocketed to 278.71 on Friday from last Friday's close of 267.72.

The market was vigorous after the four-day weekend in near record trade of 110.7 million kroons on Wednesday, spurred by reports that Sweden's Swedbank planned to up its hold in Hoiupank to 19.9 percent from its present 12 percent stake.
Swedbank confirmed on Thursday that it reached an agreement with the Estonian central bank to boost its stake in Hoiupank, which gained eight percent over the week to 152.00 kroons on the news.
Hoiupank was also pushed up by a newspaper report on Friday that it was in merger talks with Tallinna Pank.
It downplayed the report and Tallinna denied it in the afternoon, but the market had already moved.
Dealers said they expected the week's gains to be extended next week ahead of the release of six-month results from the banking sector.
LATVIA

Latvia's recently introduced bourse index closed on Friday at 383.20, up from 380.2 last Friday, but the market was laid low by the midsummer holiday and sluggish for much of the brief three-day week.
Analysts say it is still hampered by a lack of large companies and liquidity and mostly divorced from trends elsewhere in Europe and the region.
The money that is available is being channeled into privatisation vouchers ahead of the sell-off of key state assets, dealers say.
One of the few bright spots was Unibanka, which seemed to stabilse at 3.35 lats.
Dealers say that Unibanka, the traditional anchor for the bourse, could keep the rest of the market from sinking too far.
LITHUANIA
Lithuania was the only Baltic market opened all week but like Latvia it was diminished by the midsummer festivities.
The official list index, which tracks its five top blue chips, slid from 897.5 points last Friday to 884.41 points but rallied over 14 points on Friday to close at 898.52.
The group A index finished slightly down at 1,873.69 on Friday compared to 1,876.94 last Friday.
The market has been in the throes of a long and painful correction since a January bull-run which pushed shares to historic highs and the group A index to over 3,200.
That correction has scared off local investors and low liquidity and relatively poor transparancy has made foreign investors wary.
Block trades reached two million litas on Friday but the central market turnover was low for much of the week.
Dealers say that low prices may intice buyers back to the market but the summer is expected to keep a lid on turnover.
